title: Microfluidic Buffer Exchange for Interference-free Micro/Nanoparticle Cell Engineering
protocol: Culture mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) in Dulbecco's modified Eagle's medium (DMEM) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) and antibiotics to ≥80% confluency.
Culture THP-1 cells in Roswell Park Memorial Institute (RPMI) 1640 medium supplemented with 10% FBS to a density of ~10^6 cells/ml.
Load silica nanoparticles (~500 µm) with calcein dye solution (200 µM) using overnight stirring.
Dissolve 250 µg of CAM and 100 mg PLGA (50:50) in chloroform at 4 °C.
Generate single emulsion nanoparticles using a high speed homogenizer (13,600 x g, 60 sec) at room temperature.
Evaporate the chloroform in a chemical hood (≥3 hr).
Collect NPs using centrifugation (3,400 x g for 5 min), washing with double distilled water.
Freeze-dry and store the nanoparticles in -20 °C.
Incubate CAM-PLGA NPs (1 mg) or calcein silica NPs (150 µg) in 0.01% poly-L-lysine (PLL) solution at room temperature for 15 - 20 min.
Centrifuge the mixture at 3,400 x g for 5 min to remove excess PLL supernatant.
Resuspend NPs in 1 ml of respective culture medium.
Incubate the nanoparticles with cells (MSCs or THP-1, ~1 - 2 x 10^6 cells in total) for approximately 24 hr at a labeling concentration of 0.1 mg/ml.
Dissociate adherent MSCs using 2 ml of 0.25% trypsin at 37 °C for 5 min.
Quench the dissociation with 6 ml of DMEM.
Spin down the cells at 1,000 x g for 4 min.
Resuspend the cells to a concentration of 10^5 - 10^6 cells/ml for microfluidic processing.
Use labeled THP-1 cells directly at a concentration of 10^5 - 10^6 cells/ml for microfluidics purification.
Mix 30 g of PDMS base prepolymer with 3 g curing agent thoroughly in a weighing boat.
De-gas the mixture in a desiccator for 60 min to remove air bubbles.
Pour the PDMS mixture onto the silicon wafer master mold patterned with the spiral channel design carefully to a height of ~5 - 10 mm.
De-gas the mixture again in a desiccator vacuum for 60 min to remove any remaining air bubbles.
Cure the PDMS mixture in an 80 °C oven for 2 hours until set.
Cut out the PDMS spiral device using a scalpel.
Peel the PDMS slab from the master mold carefully.
Trim the edges of the device with a scalpel to ensure smooth bonding surfaces.
Punch two holes (1.5 mm) on each side of the PDMS device for inlets and outlets using a 1.5 mm biopsy puncher.
Wash the device with isopropanol (IPA) to remove any debris.
Dry the device in an 80 °C oven for 5 min.
Clean the bottom surface of the PDMS device using masking tape.
Clean one side of a glass slide using masking tape.
Place the cleaned surfaces of the PDMS device and glass slide in the chamber of a plasma cleaner.
Subject them to vacuum for 60 sec.
Switch on the plasma power to maximum.
Lower the chamber pressure until the chamber turns pink in color.
Expose the surfaces to air plasma for 60 sec.
Turn off the plasma power after exposure.
Release the pressure from the plasma cleaner to retrieve the device and glass slide.
Press the plasma-exposed surfaces of PDMS device and glass slide tightly together.
Ensure no bubbles are trapped between the two surfaces when bonding.
Heat the bonded device using a hotplate set at 80 °C for 2 hr to strengthen the bonding.
Cut two pieces of tubing (1.52 mm OD) of ~15 - 20 cm for the inlet syringes.
Attach a syringe tip (gauge 23) on one end of each tubing.
Cut two pieces of tubing (1.52 mm OD) of ~5 - 10 cm for the outlets.
Attach the shorter tubing to the outlet holes of the PDMS device.
Prime the device with a syringe containing 70% ethanol until it flows out of the outlet tubing.
Allow the ethanol to sit for 30 seconds to 1 minute to sterilize the device.
Load 30 ml of filtered (0.2 µm pore) sheath buffer into the 60 ml syringe and secure it on a syringe pump.
Set the syringe pump to Syringe size: 60 ml, Volume: 60,000 µl.
Load 3 ml of labeled cells into the 3 ml syringe and secure it on a separate syringe pump.
Set the second syringe pump to Syringe size: 3 ml, Volume: 3,000 µl.
Check that no air bubbles are trapped in either syringe.
Remove any air bubbles by gently ejecting few drops of liquid out of the nozzle.
Connect the inlet syringe tips and tubing to the syringes and insert them into the respective inlets of the device (sheath and sample inlet).
Ensure there are no bubbles along the tubing.
Mount the devices onto an inverted phase-contrast microscope for real-time imaging during cell sorting process.
Secure a small waste beaker and two 15 ml tubes close to the device on the microscope stage using adhesives.
Place the outlet tubings into the waste beaker.
Set the flow ratio for sample to sheath buffer to 1:10.
Start both syringe pumps to initiate the sorting process.
Run the device for 1.5 min for the flow rate to stabilize.

Confirm stabilization by presence of inertially focused cells near the channel inner wall under bright-field with phase contrast using a high-speed camera (~5,000 - 10,000 frames per second (fps), exposure time: 10-50 µsec).
Position the outlet tubings into different tubes to collect the eluents from the cell outlet and waste outlet.
